top_choice_rationale: P002 (Cullis, Madden, Hope; ionizable lipid nanoparticles) is the most mature achievement on the slate: a general physical-chemical design principle (pH-dependent charge, packing and non-bilayer phase behaviour, controlled mixing) that is quantitatively testable, independently reproduced for decades, and validated by approved siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines at pandemic scale. The Vancouver line established the ionizable-lipid concept, low-pH encapsulation and reproducible formulation before the lipidoid libraries, so each name maps to an identifiable step, and the citation is scoped to design and formulation. The attribution against Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan remains a real cost. P001 follows because the induced-proximity mechanism is structurally well supported and cereblon is clinically validated, but no PROTAC is approved and the trio omits Ciulli and Sakamoto. P003 is clean and mature but reads as an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize. A prize is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I work on lipid self-assembly and membranes and am scientifically close to P002, and I am a Lund colleague of Linke and Somfai, but I have no connection to any credited laureate.
